line: The Tree of the ten sephiroth as Crowley draws it, as Jung names it, and as von Franz reads the ten numbers.

sections.title: The Qabalistic Tree (Crowley)
sections.line: Crowley calls the Tree a map of the Universe, its essence the Sephiroth, and divides its numbers into four planes matched to the four elements.

quotes.quote: This picture represents the Tree of Life, which is a map of the Universe.
Hitherto, the main theme of this essay has been the Tree of Life, in its essence the Sephiroth.
numbers 4 to 9, to Air; and the number 10 to Earth.
The number I is Atziluth, the Archetypal World

sections.title: In Jung
sections.line: Jung names the Tree in the Adam Kadmon passages and in his notes on the ten. Beyond Yesod's ninth place he does not number the sephiroth.

quotes.quote: Kether, the Crown, corresponds to the upward-growing root of the Tree of the Sefiroth
in the usual arrangement of the Sefiroth he occupies the second place
Adam Kadmon is either the whole tree or is thought of as the mediator between the supreme authority, En Soph, and the Sefiroth
has parallels with the Cabalistic tree of the Sefiroth
divided into three parts (three columns of three Sefiroth each)

sections.title: The ten as the numbers
sections.line: Jung calls the numbers one to ten a completed cycle; von Franz calls the ten primal numbers the sephiroth, spheres of the unknowable primal one. Each quotation keeps its own voice.

quotes.quote: Ten is the perfect unfolding of unity, and the numbers one to ten have the significance of a completed cycle
in which ten here signifies the whole inexhaustible multiplicity of existence
the ten primal numbers, the sephiroth, are considered to be emanations of divine immaterial origin
They are “spheres” and “totalities” of the unknowable primal one

sections.title: The Abyss and Daath (Crowley)
sections.line: Daath and the Abyss are not sephiroth and have no family of their own. Crowley places the Abyss between the Ideal and the Actual, and Daath as the false sephira.

quotes.quote: For below the Abyss, contradiction is division; but above the Abyss, contradiction is Unity.
Saturn is in the position of the non‐existent Sephira, Daäth,
still less the false Sephira, Da’ath, knowledge.
